options.text: Sends data to a server called body
Renders its children at a different DOM location (the body) while keeping them logically in your component

questions.explanation: Teleport moves where children are rendered in the DOM (e.g. to <body>) but keeps their state, props, and events tied to the original component.

questions.prompt: Why is Teleport useful for modals and tooltips?

options.text: It lets them escape an ancestor's overflow: hidden or z-index stacking context

questions.explanation: Rendering to <body> frees the overlay from ancestor clipping and stacking, a common cause of cut-off or mis-layered modals.

options.text: Async dependencies in its subtree, showing a #fallback until they resolve

questions.explanation: Suspense waits for async descendants (async setup or async components) and displays the #fallback slot until they're ready, then shows #default.

questions.prompt: As of the current docs, Suspense is still marked ______ (its API may change). (one word)
questions.explanation: Suspense is an experimental feature; its API could change, so use it deliberately.

questions.prompt: Does Teleport change a component's logical parent?

options.text: Yes, it reparents the component entirely
No — it only moves the DOM location; props, events, and reactivity behave as if in place

questions.explanation: Teleport changes where content renders in the DOM, not the component hierarchy — the teleported content stays logically part of your component.

questions.prompt: What happens if a Teleport's target selector doesn't exist in the DOM?

options.text: The content has nowhere to render and Vue warns — ensure the target exists (e.g. body)
It renders on the server instead

questions.explanation: The teleport target must exist when the Teleport mounts. Teleporting to body (which always exists) or ensuring the target is present avoids the warning.
